title: A1.1 Lesson 1: Water: Polarity, Hydrogen Bonding, Cohesion and Adhesion

1.title: Water as the medium for life

q.1: 1. State where the first cells originated, and suggest one reason why life began there rather than on dry land.
q.2: 2. List four reasons why life depends on water. Beside each one write a single sentence saying why it matters to a cell or an organism.

2.title: Atoms, bonds and the water molecule

q.Table: 3. Complete the table for the three particles in an atom.
q.4(a): 4(a). Outline how an ionic bond forms between a sodium atom and a chlorine atom.
q.4(b): 4(b). Outline how a covalent bond forms between an oxygen atom and a hydrogen atom.
q.5(a): 5(a). State where the polar covalent bonds are found in a water molecule.
q.5(b): 5(b). Explain why the electrons in an O–H bond are not shared equally, and why this gives the oxygen a partial negative charge and each hydrogen a partial positive charge.
q.6(a): 6(a). Outline what causes a hydrogen bond to form between two water molecules.
q.6(b): 6(b). A single hydrogen bond is weak. Outline two consequences of the collective strength of the many hydrogen bonds in liquid water.

q.8: 8. Describe how water moves through the xylem of a vascular plant, from the root to the leaf.
q.9(a): 9(a). Outline the cause of surface tension.
q.9(b): 9(b). State one benefit to living things that results from surface tension.

q.10: 10. Define each of these terms: adhesion, polar, ion.
q.11: 11. Compare a cation with an anion.
q.12: 12. Explain why water is attracted to molecules that are polar or charged.
q.13(b): 13(b). Describe capillary action in plant tissue.
q.13(c): 13(c). Outline the cause and one effect of capillary action in soil.

q.14: 14. Explain how the polarity of a water molecule leads to hydrogen bonding, and how hydrogen bonding gives rise to both cohesion and adhesion.
q.15: 15. Water reaches the leaves of a redwood tree 100 m tall, with no pump of any kind. Explain how, using the terms transpiration, cohesion and adhesion.
